entities.name: Orestes of Macedon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Orestes, a scion of the Argead dynasty, briefly held the throne of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon from approximately 400/399 BCE to 398/397 BCE. As the son of the powerful and innovative King Archelaus I, his short reign represents a critical, albeit tumultuous, interlude in Macedon's transition from a peripheral Balkan kingdom to a dominant Hellenic power. His ascendance and rapid demise underscore the intense dynastic struggles and political fragilities that characterized the Macedonian monarchy in the early 4th century BCE, setting a precedent for the ruthless power contests that would define the kingdom prior to Philip II's consolidation of power.

Following the assassination of his father, Archelaus I, in 399 BCE, Orestes, then a minor, was placed under the regency of Aeropus II, a prominent figure within the Macedonian aristocracy, possibly his uncle. The exact circumstances of Archelaus's death are debated, with some sources suggesting a palace conspiracy involving Aeropus himself. Orestes's reign was largely titular, overshadowed by Aeropus's effective control. Historical accounts, primarily from Diodorus Siculus, indicate that Aeropus either assassinated or deposed Orestes after a mere two years on the throne, consolidating sole power for himself by 398/397 BCE. This act of regicide or usurpation effectively ended the direct line of succession from Archelaus I through his son, plunging Macedon into further instability.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Orestes's brief and violent reign, ending in his deposition or murder, typified the extreme political instability and dynastic struggles that plagued Macedon for decades after Archelaus I, hindering its development until Philip II's consolidation of power.
